Quickstart

\n

The fastest path from zero to a running pipeline.

\n\n

1. Get an API key

\n

See Authentication if you don't have one yet.

\n\n

2. Create a pipeline

\n{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\\\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\" \\\\\\n -d '{\"name\":\"my-first-pipeline\",\"source_connector_id\":\"conn_demo_source\",\"destination_connector_id\":\"conn_demo_dest\"}'}}\n\n

3. Watch it run

\n

Subscribe to pipeline.completed via Webhooks, or poll the Events endpoint to see events as they're processed.

\n\n{{ds:component/alert|variant=success|title=That's it|body_html=

For a fuller walkthrough with a real source and destination, go to Building your first pipeline in the Guides section.

}}\n\n{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/0d0c5a67-ddfd-45fa-b23c-796c67d5784e}}|prev_label=Installation|next_href={{cms:item/67e28ef9-df46-446a-9839-8f4bd0b23de1}}|next_label=Authentication}}", "version_token": "0fc2836d-2afc-427a-9662-5919684cf85b", "created_at": "2026-08-21T04:51:26.349Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-21T04:51:36.184Z", "placement_id": "92f88acb-393a-4efd-bb47-cc71ee93a4d8", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "getting-started-quickstart" } }

{ "item": { "id": "7de0fdb1-6046-47d5-afc5-dc00a8f02c79", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Authentication", "short_description": "Authenticate API requests with a bearer API key.", "body": "

Authentication

\n

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

\n\n

Getting an API key

\n

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits & errors.

\n\n

Using the key

\n{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\\\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}\n\n{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}\n\n

Verifying webhook requests

\n

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

\n\n{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/1aaa9856-f563-4263-929f-16e234970286}}|prev_label=Quickstart|next_href={{cms:item/2df76640-838b-4256-956e-d8a19a602241}}|next_label=Building your first pipeline}}", "version_token": "d89d4dc3-2f2d-40c2-a9e8-9a44635d7d4f", "created_at": "2026-08-21T04:42:06.192Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-21T04:43:04.598Z", "placement_id": "a8665e39-d994-43d7-9f40-791673ac7d44", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "getting-started-authentication" } }

{ "item": { "id": "ca08f5db-0003-4cb7-9bde-4b92ef8f24b2", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Building your first pipeline", "short_description": "Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.", "body": "

Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

You'll need an API key. See Authentication in Getting Started if you don't have one yet.

}}

1. Create a source connector

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\\n -d '{"type":"postgres","direction":"source","config":{"connection_string":"postgres://..."}}'}}

2. Create a destination connector

We'll write to Snowflake.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\\n -d '{"type":"snowflake","direction":"destination","config":{"account":"..."}}'}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\\n -d '{"name":"ingest-orders","source_connector_id":"conn_pg_orders","destination_connector_id":"conn_snowflake_dw"}'}}

The pipeline starts in draft state. Activate it once you're ready to start processing events.

Next steps

Now that events are flowing, read Handling errors & retries to see what happens when a write fails, or Monitoring & alerts to watch it run.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/60d7d27a-ceda-4034-b98e-8b1181ca5c84}}|prev_label=Guides|next_href={{cms:item/3448ffab-598c-46e7-bda6-e7cdc4a1e7c6}}|next_label=Connecting a data source}}", "version_token": "a11c157a-7635-4b93-b8e4-bb20b368126a", "created_at": "2026-08-21T04:50:47.701Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-21T04:51:36.070Z", "placement_id": "546623a3-eb81-48dc-8562-eb2751ef9082", "folder_id": "c3e0ba4a-a491-4265-9848-556d298e6b6b", "file_name": "building-your-first-pipeline" } }

content.text: Now I'll update the three pages with Go code examples:

input.body:
Quickstart

The fastest path from zero to a running pipeline.

1. Get an API key

See Authentication if you don't have one yet.

2. Create a pipeline

Bash

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\ -d '{\"name\":\"my-first-pipeline\",\"source_connector_id\":\"conn_demo_source\",\"destination_connector_id\":\"conn_demo_dest\"}'}}

Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "log" "os" "github.com/godzilla-io/godzilla-go/client" ) func main() { apiKey := os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY") c := client.New(apiKey) pipeline, err := c.Pipelines.Create(context.Background(), &client.CreatePipelineRequest{ Name: "my-first-pipeline", SourceConnectorID: "conn_demo_source", DestinationConnectorID: "conn_demo_dest", }) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("failed to create pipeline: %v", err) } log.Printf("created pipeline: %s", pipeline.ID) }}}

3. Watch it run

Subscribe to pipeline.completed via Webhooks, or poll the Events endpoint to see events as they're processed.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=success|title=That's it|body_html=

For a fuller walkthrough with a real source and destination, go to Building your first pipeline in the Guides section.

}} {{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/0d0c5a67-ddfd-45fa-b23c-796c67d5784e}}|prev_label=Installation|next_href={{cms:item/67e28ef9-df46-446a-9839-8f4bd0b23de1}}|next_label=Authentication}}

Authentication

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

Getting an API key

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits & errors.

Using the key

Bash

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}}

Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "github.com/godzilla-io/godzilla-go/client" ) func main() { apiKey := os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY") c := client.New(apiKey) pipelines, err := c.Pipelines.List(context.Background()) if err != nil { panic(err) } for _, p := range pipelines { fmt.Printf("Pipeline: %s (ID: %s)\n", p.Name, p.ID) } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}

Verifying webhook requests

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/1aaa9856-f563-4263-929f-16e234970286}}|prev_label=Quickstart|next_href={{cms:item/2df76640-838b-4256-956e-d8a19a602241}}|next_label=Building your first pipeline}}

Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

You'll need an API key. See Authentication in Getting Started if you don't have one yet.

}}

1. Create a source connector

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

Bash

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \\ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\ -d '{\"type\":\"postgres\",\"direction\":\"source\",\"config\":{\"connection_string\":\"postgres://...\"}}'}}

Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_connector.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "log" "os" "github.com/godzilla-io/godzilla-go/client" ) func createSourceConnector(ctx context.Context, c *client.Client) (string, error) { connector, err := c.Connectors.Create(ctx, &client.CreateConnectorRequest{ Type: "postgres", Direction: "source", Config: map[string]interface{}{ "connection_string": "postgres://...", }, }) return connector.ID, err }}}

2. Create a destination connector

We'll write to Snowflake.

Bash

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \\ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\ -d '{\"type\":\"snowflake\",\"direction\":\"destination\",\"config\":{\"account\":\"...\"}}'}}

Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_connector.go|language=go|code=func createDestinationConnector(ctx context.Context, c *client.Client) (string, error) { connector, err := c.Connectors.Create(ctx, &client.CreateConnectorRequest{ Type: "snowflake", Direction: "destination", Config: map[string]interface{}{ "account": "...", }, }) return connector.ID, err }}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

Bash

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \\ -d '{\"name\":\"ingest-orders\",\"source_connector_id\":\"conn_pg_orders\",\"destination_connector_id\":\"conn_snowflake_dw\"}'}}

Go

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_pipeline.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "context" "log" "os" "github.com/godzilla-io/godzilla-go/client" ) func main() { apiKey := os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY") c := client.New(apiKey) pipeline, err := c.Pipelines.Create(context.Background(), &client.CreatePipelineRequest{ Name: "ingest-orders", SourceConnectorID: "conn_pg_orders", DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw", }) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("failed to create pipeline: %v", err) } log.Printf("created pipeline: %s (state: %s)", pipeline.ID, pipeline.State) }}}

The pipeline starts in draft state. Activate it once you're ready to start processing events.

Next steps

Now that events are flowing, read Handling errors & retries to see what happens when a write fails, or Monitoring & alerts to watch it run.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/60d7d27a-ceda-4034-b98e-8b1181ca5c84}}|prev_label=Guides|next_href={{cms:item/3448ffab-598c-46e7-bda6-e7cdc4a1e7c6}}|next_label=Connecting a data source}}

content.text:
Perfect! I've successfully added Go code examples to all three pages. Here's what I did:

## Summary

I've added Go SDK code examples alongside the existing bash/curl examples on three key pages:

### **Quickstart** 
- Added a Go example showing how to create a pipeline using the `godzilla-go` SDK client

### **Authentication**
- Added a Go example demonstrating how to authenticate and list pipelines using the SDK

### **Building your first pipeline**
- Added Go examples for all three steps:
  1. Creating a source connector (Postgres)
  2. Creating a destination connector (Snowflake)
  3. Creating the pipeline

Each example demonstrates idiomatic Go patterns like error handling, context usage, and the SDK's client API. The code is positioned logically after the bash examples, making it easy for Go developers to find the equivalent SDK calls.

**Staging URL:** https://staging.localhost:4310  
**Review URL:** http://localhost:3001/sites/32114acb-ccbe-44e4-96d4-64fa594284e2/change-sets/60406e2e-2c71-4f35-b7af-f9ca600d8a04

A human reviewer will now review the changes in the RIFT interface before they go live.
